title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
Waymo's autonomous vehicles proved unable to handle extended periods of severe traffic congestion on San Francisco streets during Fourth of July celebrations. Multiple vehicles ran out of battery while stuck in gridlock, with at least a dozen requiring recovery. The system was deployed in conditions—major holiday traffic and road closures—that exceeded its designed operating range, and the vehicles lacked either sufficient battery capacity for such scenarios or a means to alert passengers and request manual intervention before becoming immobilized.

One vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks on the roadway, and a passenger reported the vehicle continued driving when fireworks ignited nearby. The incident shows that the autonomous system either could not detect or could not properly respond to hazardous road debris and fire hazards. It is not established whether the fire started because of a failure to detect the debris, a failure to avoid it, or some other mechanical cause.

The deployment lacked a safeguard that would have prevented this: advance planning for battery drain during foreseeable congestion, either through route planning that avoids such conditions or through explicit intervention protocols when traffic is abnormally heavy. Waymo stated it is evaluating improvements to resilience during major traffic events.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
Several Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded on San Francisco streets after their batteries drained during severe traffic congestion following Fourth of July fireworks celebrations. Video footage showed at least a dozen stationary Waymo vehicles, primarily Jaguar I-PEACE models, lined up on streets near the Golden Gate Bridge. The company attributed the gridlock to major traffic disruptions, high volumes of travelers, and unplanned road closures. Some vehicles required towing, and one caught fire after driving over fireworks that were set off in the road. One passenger reported the vehicle continued driving when fireworks ignited nearby.

Waymo stated it is evaluating ways to improve resilience during major traffic events. San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie's office announced plans to discuss the incident with stakeholders to improve future experiences. This incident follows a December outage when power failures caused some Waymo vehicles to stop at malfunctioning traffic lights. The city's emergency management department had warned residents about heavy traffic and crowded transit conditions after the fireworks display.
